# Editor gaps that FuzzEditorConsistency's sample of cases and documentation
# snippets reaches on main: relations between language server answers that
# LSP 3.17 and Chapter 28's "Rewrites keep meaning" (D372) require. Each key's
# minimal reproductions are listed by corpus file, so that each fails as XPASS
# once fixed, and the fix deletes its key's lines.
# <target> <key> <owner> <what is missing, with the decision it breaks>
FuzzEditorConsistency consistency:rename:VariableDeclaration:diagnostics:TS2339 compiler D372: renaming a shorthand binding element whose default is a `do` block that returns, as in `const { n = do { return 7 } } = o` in any function or the same pattern in a `for concurrent` head, writes `{ fresh = … }` instead of `{ n: fresh = … }`, so the pattern reads another property and the rename adds TS2339 (snippet rejectedHeads, docs/design/src/002-running.md)

FuzzEditorConsistency corpus:rename-do-default-shorthand-for-concurrent compiler D372: renaming a shorthand binding element whose default is a `do` block that returns, as in `const { n = do { return 7 } } = o` in any function or the same pattern in a `for concurrent` head, writes `{ fresh = … }` instead of `{ n: fresh = … }`, so the pattern reads another property and the rename adds TS2339 (snippet rejectedHeads, docs/design/src/002-running.md)
FuzzEditorConsistency consistency:call-hierarchy:outgoing-missing:ClassDeclaration compiler LSP 3.17: a call in a class member's computed name, as in `class Call { [key()]: number = 1 }` or `error Call { [key()]: number }`, is among `key`'s incoming calls from `Call` but not among `Call`'s outgoing calls, because the call hierarchy collects a class's computed member names as calls of the enclosing declaration (case error-declarations-native-key-shapes.fail)

FuzzEditorConsistency corpus:calls-error-computed-key compiler LSP 3.17: a call in a class member's computed name, as in `class Call { [key()]: number = 1 }` or `error Call { [key()]: number }`, is among `key`'s incoming calls from `Call` but not among `Call`'s outgoing calls, because the call hierarchy collects a class's computed member names as calls of the enclosing declaration (case error-declarations-native-key-shapes.fail)
